To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

free probability theory can be applied to channel capacity estimation and that it can be used to derive unbiased channel capacity estimators for MIMO channels, which are also unbiased for MIMO channels with frequency drift and phase off-set.

we have introduced a new estimator for the capacity of MIMO channels impaired by noise, and that we have also introduced a new estimator of the capacity of MIMOC channels impaired by both phase off-set and drift.

free probability can be applied to estimate the capacity of MIMO channels, and that the free-probabiity-based and the Gaussian-matrix-mean based estimators provide unbiased estimates of the channel capacity and moments of the channel matrices.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of channel capacity estimation for MIMO channels with noise and/or phase off-set and/or frequency drift, and we have shown that free probability can be a useful tool for this purpose.
the development of an efficient estimator for the capacity of the MIMO fading channel with phase off-set, frequency drift, and additive white Gaussian noise, based on the free-probabilistic approach.
the application of free probability to wireless communication problems, and in particular to the problem of channel capacity estimation in a MIMO system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
free probability is a useful and promising tool for channel capacity estimation.
the two estimators provide asymptotically unbiased estimation for the capacity of MIMO channels impaired by noise, phase off-set, and frequency drift.

free probability provides a powerful tool for estimating the channel capacity of MIMO systems, and the two estimators introduced here are the best available estimators for the capacity estimation in the presence of noise, and in the presence of both noise and phase off-set and/or frequency drift, respectively.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have introduced a novel estimator for MIMO channel capacity and provided a theoretical analysis of its properties.
we have provided a new approach to estimate the capacity of MIMO channels using the tools of free probability.
the proposed estimators are useful for capacity estimation in many practical scenarios, especially when a low number of observations is available.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Gaussian matrix-mean estimator is a useful estimator for MIMO channel capacity estimation, even for a low number antennas and samples, and can be extended to more complicated channel models such as MIMO channels with frequency drift and phase off-set.
the Gaussian matrix-mean estimator can be used for estimating the moments of the MIMO channel matrix in a large class of MIMO systems.
free probability is an extremely powerful tool for capacity estimation of MIMO channels.
